title: Cabin Addition on Summit Retro Credits
content:
On a retro credit in the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program, the fare brand of the credited ticket decides a cabin addition to the miles the credit carries. The fare brand is read from the ticket's own record under the Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand charter.

**Rule.** A Crestline First ticket adds the premium cabin bonus percent that the Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand charter sets for Crestline First; a Crestline Premium Economy ticket adds the premium cabin bonus percent that the same charter sets for Crestline Premium Economy; a ticket of any other fare brand adds no cabin addition. That charter's premium cabin bonus percent is the bonus award miles on a flown coupon of the fare brand, as a percent of the base award miles. The percent is taken of the credit's base miles, which are the eligible fare multiplied by the award miles per dollar of the tier the member holds on the day the credit posts, rounded to the nearest whole mile with halves rounded up. The addition itself is rounded to the nearest whole mile, halves rounded up, and is added to the miles the retro credit carries.

| Fare brand of the credited ticket | Percent applied to the base miles |
|---|---|
| Crestline First | Premium cabin bonus percent set for Crestline First |
| Crestline Premium Economy | Premium cabin bonus percent set for Crestline Premium Economy |
| Crestline Basic Economy, Main Cabin, Main Plus or Main Flexible | None (0 percent) |

**Hypothetical worked figure.** A retro credit with 2231 base miles on a Crestline Premium Economy ticket, taking a hypothetical premium cabin bonus percent of 40 for that brand: 40 percent of 2231 is 892.4, rounded to 892 miles added. The same credit on a Crestline Main Plus ticket adds nothing.

**Half-mile case (hypothetical).** 30 percent of 1235 base miles is 370.5, which rounds up to 371.
